items.title: Farm animals and a ‘unicorn’ coming to Mississauga
items.summary: Parents looking for something a little different to do with the kids this fall can head to Port Credit later this month for an afternoon of farm animals, crafts, entertainment, and a rather unusual prize. Fall’N The Port is taking over Brant Avenue on Saturday, Oct. m. One of the biggest attractions for kids could be the chance to meet a collection of farm animals, including alpacas, goats, rabbits and a donkey. There will also be face painting, crafts and live entertainment from buskers, giving families plenty to see and do as they explore Port Credit. But perhaps the most intriguing part of the afternoon will require a little detective work. Event organizers are hiding 30 scarecrows throughout participating Port Credit businesses, and families are invited to hunt them down. Visitors can pick up a scarecrow hunt map at the BIA tent before setting out through the neighbourhood to find and identify all 30. Those who complete the hunt can enter a draw for a Family Prize Pack and the grand prize comes with an especially memorable experience: a chance to ride a unicorn…or at least a reasonable facsimile.

items.title: Marvel star, Mississauga’s Simu Liu got married in France
items.summary: Marvel star Simu Liu, who grew up in Mississauga, got married in France on the weekend, according to reports. Liu, 37, married Allison Hsu, 30 over the weekend of Oct. 3, according to multiple news reports. The couple announced their engagement in Paris in May 2025. “From weekends in Paris, day trips to Palm Springs, long nights on set, afternoons vegging on the couch and everything in between, I choose you forever and always,” Liu said in the engagement announcement. Starting out in the acclaimed Canadian television show, Kim’s Convenience, Liu’s career blew up after his starring role in the 2021 Marvel film Shang-Chi and the Legend of the Ten Rings. His most recent role is in the new TV science fiction spy thriller series The Copenhagen Test. He is also in the upcoming Avengers: Doomsday, which is in post-production. Hsu is the vice president of digital marketing at Interscope Records. The couple has been dating since late 2022. She posted photos from what appears to be a bachelorette party in Mexico in September. Born in Harbin, China, Liu came to Canada when he was five years old. His parents bought a home in a new residential development off of Winston Churchill Boulevard, and Liu attended Thorn Lodge Public School. He was inducted into Mississauga’s Legends Row, the city’s Walk of Fame, in 2024.

items.title: Man arrested after campaign volunteer in Mississauga threatened with knife while installing election sign
items.summary: A volunteer with a Mississauga mayoral candidate was threatened with a knife while they were installing a sign on Monday night, police say. m. on Monday in the area of Truscott Drive and Southdown Road, according to a spokesperson for Alvin Tedjo’s campaign. Peel Regional Police say a 60-year-old male suspect threatened the volunteer with a knife before the victim disarmed him. The victim sustained minor injuries, police said. The suspect, who has not been identified by police, was charged with assault with a weapon. He was released on an undertaking and is scheduled to appear in the Ontario Court of Justice at a later date, police said. Tedjo addressed the incident in a statement on Tuesday, noting that the volunteer “was confronted by a stranger and attacked” while installing campaign signs. “I have spoken with the victim to offer my support as they recover from this altercation. items.title: Missing six-year-old Whitby girl found in Mississauga
items.summary: A missing six-year-old girl who was last seen in Whitby over the weekend has been found in Mississauga and is now safe and sound, Durham Regional Police say. m. on Saturday, Oct. 3, near Dundas Street and Thickson Road in Whitby. Her disappearance prompted a wide search by police and a call for assistance to the media and the public. Shortly after noon today, police took to social media to confirm that the child had been located. Police did not release any additional details about the circumstances surrounding her disappearance, but a spokesman for Durham Police said she was found in Mississauga “with the assistance of the media and some information from the public” in the company of Blair Hamilton, a friend of her father’s. “She will be assessed and medically cleared, and we will be interviewing the man she was with,” the spokesman said. Hamilton has not been charged with any offence in this case and police said that an investigation into the incident is still ongoing. ” “We want to recognize and thank everyone involved for contributing to a positive and successful outcome,” police said on X.

items.title: Zoocasa Data Shows Mississauga's Cheapest Home Sales Last Month All Came In Under $400,000
items.summary: According to real estate brokerage Zoocasa, the five least expensive homes sold in Mississauga last month all closed under $400,000, with the cheapest going for $350,000. The Toronto Regional Real Estate Board reported home prices across the Greater Toronto Area fell roughly 1 per cent year-over-year in September, continuing a sluggish stretch for the market. Zoocasa's list shows a one-bedroom-plus-den condo in downtown Erin Mills sold for $390,000, under its asking price, offering panoramic views, an open-concept layout and amenities including an indoor pool, gym and yoga studio. Another entry, a 665-square-foot one-bedroom-plus-den unit in City Centre, features 10-foot ceilings and floor-to-ceiling windows and includes a parking space and locker. Insauga reports buyers willing to consider smaller condo units can still find homes well below the city's typical price point even as the broader market stays soft.

items.title: Peel Police Say Retail Theft Charges Already Near 2025's Full-Year Total With Four Months Left
items.summary: According to Insauga, Peel Regional Police have laid 2,241 retail theft-related charges in the first eight months of 2026, just 69 shy of the 2,310 charges laid during all of 2025. Deputy Chief Marc Andrews shared the figures Tuesday as Peel Police hosted a two-day conference in Mississauga on organized retail crime. Andrews said the current pace puts the region on track to surpass 3,300 charges by year's end if the rate holds through December. He said the numbers reflect more than scattered shoplifting, describing a pattern that is, in his words, far more coordinated, sophisticated and far-reaching than before. Andrews said investigators are increasingly finding that crimes once treated as isolated incidents are tied to the same repeat offenders and organized networks operating well beyond a single community.

items.title: Peel Schools Skip the Early PA Day This Year, Leaving Oct. 12 as Students' Only Extra Day Off Until Late October
items.summary: According to Mississauga.com, students in the Peel District School Board and the Dufferin-Peel Catholic District School Board will get Monday, Oct. 12 off for the Thanksgiving statutory holiday, giving them a three-day weekend. Unlike some other Ontario school boards, neither Peel board added a Professional Activity day on the Friday before the long weekend to stretch it further. Mississauga.com reports the two boards' 2026-27 calendars otherwise line up closely, with students' next scheduled day off being a PA day on Monday, Oct. 26. The outlet says families can find the full breakdown of PA days, March break and exam schedules in each board's calendar for the school year. The three-day weekend applies to elementary and secondary students across Mississauga, Brampton and Caledon.

items.title: Mississauga Road Reopens After Overnight Crash Leaves One Driver in Critical Condition
items.summary: According to Insauga, one driver was left in critical condition after a two-vehicle crash on Mississauga Road near Featherston Drive on Monday night. Peel Regional Police said both drivers were injured and taken to a local trauma centre following the collision. The crash happened at the intersection with Featherston Drive, prompting police to close Mississauga Road between Burnhamthorpe Road West and Harkiss Road. Insauga reports the road has since reopened to traffic. Police have not released further details on what caused the collision.
